The page: 'Their claim, which was made in 1848' rested on Ternate's tributary ties to Papua, and Tidore recognised Dutch sovereignty in 1872; the first administrative posts (Fakfak, Manokwari) date from 5 February 1898 and the Bird's Head was brought under Dutch administration in 1920. A claim, not a possession, until then.

region.text: Aceh

ledger.note: 26 March 1873: the Dutch attack Aceh. An expedition under Köhler 'was sent out on 26 March 1873' and bombarded Banda Aceh; the Dutch occupied most coastal areas by April. The Sumatra Treaty of 1871 preceded it; van Swieten's second expedition (November 1873) took the capital in January 1874 and the Dutch declared Aceh annexed in 1874.

region.text: coastal Aceh

ledger.note: April 1873: the Dutch hold the coast of Aceh (43 cells in Cliopatria's shape), then the capital in January 1874; the rest of Aceh stays unconquered until 1904.

region.text: Bulungan with the Tidung Lands towards Tawau, as in the 1849-1878 keyframe

ledger.note: June 1878: the protectorate ends in annexation. 'Bulungan was finally incorporated into the colonial empire of the Dutch East Indies in June 1878'. Mirrors kingdom-of-bulungan /ledger/9.

region.text: Bulungan, incorporated

ledger.note: June 1878: the Dutch incorporate Bulungan (same sentence). Mirrors kingdom-of-bulungan /ledger/10 (dissolve). The cells are already in the 1873 shape as protectorate land (see the 1853 gain); the gain marks the passage to direct rule.

region.text: Bacan, Kasiruta and Mandioli round Labuha, seat of the sultanate (Amassing)

ledger.note: 1889: 'At the demise of Sultan Muhammad Sadik (1862-1889) a commission of grandees governed for many years'; 'Dutch rule was represented by a controleur after 1883'. Mirrors sultanate-of-bacan /ledger/6 (dissolve 1889).

region.text: Bacan, Kasiruta and Mandioli round Labuha, seat of the sultanate (Amassing)

ledger.note: 1889: the old line ends and Bacan is governed by Dutch officials and a commission of grandees (same sentences; the page says the last rights of the sultan in the formal administration were abolished only in 1965). Cliopatria's shape holds these cells from 1824 as vassal land. Mirrors sultanate-of-bacan /ledger/6.

region.text: the island of Lombok

ledger.note: 1894: the Dutch take Lombok. 'The island of Lombok came under Dutch control' in 1894.

region.text: Karangasem, 'added to their possessions' by the Dutch with Lombok

ledger.note: 1894: the Dutch take Karangasem. 'In 1894, the Dutch defeated the Balinese ruler of Lombok, adding both Lombok and Karangasem to their possessions'. Mirrors bali /ledger/4 (loss); Lombok is the separate gain of 1894. The radius around Amlapura is the Bali dossier's reading; Cliopatria's shape holds Karangasem only from 1908.

region.text: interior Kalimantan, West Sumatra, Jambi and Bengkulu

ledger.note: 1898: Cliopatria adds about 1,900 cells, the interior of Kalimantan (1,500), West Sumatra, Jambi and Bengkulu. The page dates only a general sweep: 'By 1900 the archipelago was considered pacified' and direct rule 'was extended throughout the rest of the archipelago from 1901 to 1910'. Confidence 1. Repair of 2026-10-19: none of Jambi's 100 cells lie in the 1898 shape (they enter in 1905 and are dated 1904 by the Jambi page); Karangasem, Lombok and the Minangkabau highlands are carried by their own events.

region.text: Aceh

ledger.note: 1904: the Aceh War ends in Dutch victory. The infobox dates the war 1873-1904 and the page says 'Most of Aceh was under Dutch control' by the end of 1904; Sultan Daud Syah capitulated in 1903; the main page has the Acehnese surrender in 1912.

region.text: the Aceh interior

ledger.note: 1904: Aceh passes under Dutch control. Van Heutsz was proclaimed governor of Aceh in 1898; Van Daalen's 1904 campaign in the Gayo and Alas regions killed at least 2,922 Acehnese; Cliopatria adds the Aceh interior only in 1914.

region.text: the Jambi sultanate

ledger.note: 1904: the Dutch end the Jambi Sultanate. 'The killing of Sultan Taha in 1904 marked the end of the Jambi Sultanate' and the Dutch 'would eventually conquer the sultanate and kill its last ruling sultan in 1904'; the page also has the sultanate annexed into the Palembang Residency in 1903. Cliopatria's shapes hold none of Jambi's 100 cells until 1905 (none in 1898, whatever the 1898 gain note says), so the 1898 keyframe carries Jambi from 1904. Mirrors sultanate-of-jambi /ledger/9 and /ledger/10 (loss and dissolve 1904).

union.text: the Sumbawa part of Cliopatria's 1626 outline: Bima and the eastern end of the island, without the Flores tribute lands
Sumbawa and Flores lands of the Bima row

region.text: Bima's Sumbawa lands and the Flores lands that Cliopatria adds in 1890

ledger.note: 1905: Bima passes under direct Dutch control. 'In 1905 Bima was turned into a "fief" (leen)' (Bima page; it does not mention 1890 or the Flores lands). Cliopatria adds 19 cells in the Lesser Sundas in 1890 (none in Bima's Sumbawa lands, which the shape holds from 1800); they are Bima's tribute lands (Manggarai and West Flores in its dossier, which ends that dependency in 1905), so the gain is dated to Bima's end year, the Sumbawa lands pass from vassal to direct control the same year, and the keyframes of 1890-1904 leave the Flores lands out. Confidence 2: the year is the page's, the Flores reading is mine.

minus.text: south-west Sulawesi, added to the Dutch East Indies shape of 1908 over that of 1905

union.text: northern South Sulawesi: the regencies of Luwu, North Luwu, East Luwu and Palopo City (infobox), the Gulf of Bone coast and foothills where Bugis settled round 1300
Wajo round the walled capital Tosora and the central lakes (the Wajo Regency of today)

region.text: south-west Sulawesi, added to the Dutch East Indies shape of 1908 over that of 1905, without Luwu and Wajo

ledger.note: 1905-1906: south-west Sulawesi is occupied. 'Southwestern Sulawesi was occupied in 1905-06.' Cliopatria draws Sulawesi from 1908. The South Sulawesi page has Bone 'completely occupied by 30 July' 1905 and Gowa attacked on 20 October 1905; Luwu and Wajo are separate gains (confidence 1) and Gowa is a vassal that passes to direct rule in 1911.

region.text: the Sumbawa part of Cliopatria's 1626 outline: Bima and the eastern end of the island, without the Flores tribute lands

ledger.note: 1905: 'In 1905 Bima was turned into a "fief" (leen) and Sultan Ibrahim had to give up the rights to foreign trade'; 'Bima was subjected to indirect colonial rule from 1908 to 1949'. Mirrors sultanate-of-bima /ledger/8.

region.text: Tidore island, the Gamrange area of south-east Halmahera and the islands close by

ledger.note: 1905: 'The title of sultan lapsed in 1905 and was replaced by a regency' (Tidore page). Mirrors sultanate-of-tidore /ledger/17 (dissolve).

region.text: Tidore island, the Gamrange area of south-east Halmahera and the islands close by

ledger.note: 1905: the regency replaces the sultan, and Tidore passes to direct Dutch control (same sentence; the page does not use the word annexation). Cliopatria's shape holds these cells from 1824 as vassal land. Mirrors sultanate-of-tidore /ledger/17.

region.text: northern South Sulawesi: the regencies of Luwu, North Luwu, East Luwu and Palopo City (infobox), the Gulf of Bone coast and foothills where Bugis settled round 1300

ledger.note: 1905: the Dutch take Luwu. The South Sulawesi page names Luwu and Wajo as 'the chief targets of the expeditions' but gives no date for either; the year is the expeditions' (Bone completely occupied by 30 July 1905) and the Luwu dossier's bridge (confidence 1). Mirrors luwu /ledger/3; Cliopatria's shape holds these cells from 1908.

region.text: Wajo round the walled capital Tosora and the central lakes (the Wajo Regency of today)

ledger.note: 1905: the Dutch take Wajo (same page, no date for Wajo; confidence 1). Mirrors wajo /ledger/3; Cliopatria's shape holds these cells from 1908.

region.text: Badung, around Denpasar and Sanur

ledger.note: 1906: the Dutch destroy the Badung royal house. 'The Dutch mounted large naval and ground assaults at the Sanur region in 1906', 'leading to the elimination of the royal house of Badung and about 1000 deaths'. Mirrors bali /ledger/5 (loss); the radius round Denpasar is the Bali dossier's reading and Cliopatria's shape holds Badung only from 1908.

region.text: Sulawesi beyond the south-west

ledger.note: 1908: Cliopatria adds the rest of Sulawesi (about 450 cells) in the sweep of 'direct colonial rule extended throughout the rest of the archipelago from 1901 to 1910'. Confidence 1.

region.text: the rest of Bali under Klungkung's Dewa Agung and the remaining kingdoms

ledger.note: April 1908: the Dutch assault on Klungkung ends Balinese rule. 'A similar massacre occurred in the face of a Dutch assault in Klungkung', 'sealing the end of the Majapahit dynasty ... and the total rule of the Dutch over Bali' (History of Bali page); the main Dutch East Indies page: 'The island of Bali was subjugated with military conquests in' 1906 and 1908, with April 1908 for the second intervention. The region is what is left of Bali after Karangasem (1894) and Badung (1906): mirrors bali /ledger/6 (loss) and /ledger/7 (dissolve).

union.text: Jum Pandan (Ujung Pandang), the fort converted into Fort Rotterdam
Somba Opu, the fortress that Speelman destroyed in June 1669, and the coast round it

region.text: the Gowa-Tallo core (Cliopatria's 1662 outline) without the Fort Rotterdam and Somba Opu cells that the VOC took in 1667 and 1669

ledger.note: 1911: Gowa loses its independence. 'In 1911 the Sultanate lost its independence after losing the war and became one of the Dutch Indies' regencies'; 'Since 1904 the Dutch colonial government had engaged in the South Sulawesi expedition'. Mirrors sultanate-of-gowa /ledger/24.

union.text: Jum Pandan (Ujung Pandang), the fort converted into Fort Rotterdam
Somba Opu, the fortress that Speelman destroyed in June 1669, and the coast round it

region.text: the Gowa-Tallo core (Cliopatria's 1662 outline) without the Fort Rotterdam and Somba Opu cells that the VOC took in 1667 and 1669

ledger.note: 1911: the vassal sultanate becomes a Dutch East Indies regency (same sentence). Mirrors sultanate-of-gowa /ledger/25 (loss). The South Sulawesi page has the Dutch attack Gowa on 20 October 1905 and besiege Alitta on 21 December 1905; the sovereignty ends in 1911 on the Gowa page.

union.text: Ternate island with Moti, Makian and the nearest Halmahera shore: the home of the kingdom

region.text: the remaining sultanate

ledger.note: 1914: the vassalage ends. 'Sultan Haji Muhammad Usman (1902-1914) made a last attempt to oppose the Dutch ... he failed and was dethroned'; infobox 'Final ruler dethroned by Dutch: 1914'.

union.text: Ternate island with Moti, Makian and the nearest Halmahera shore: the home of the kingdom

region.text: the remaining sultanate

ledger.note: 1914: the Dutch annex Ternate. 'The Sultans of Ternate and its people were never fully under Dutch control until its annexation in 1914', and 'this spelt the end of the traditional Ternatan kingdom'. Mirrors sultanate-of-ternate /ledger/14 (loss). Cliopatria's shape holds these cells from 1824; they were vassal land until now.

region.text: parts of Kalimantan and Sulawesi under Japanese control in January 1942

ledger.note: January 1942: Japan invades the Indies. The invasion began on 10 January 1942 (the infobox gives 11 January for the occupation) and parts of Sulawesi and Kalimantan were under Japanese control that month; Cliopatria's 1942 shape lacks 191 cells in Borneo and North Sulawesi.

region.text: Sumatra and Dutch Timor

ledger.note: February 1942: Japanese forces land on Sumatra (month only) and, on 19 February, on Timor after taking Ambon; the Eastern Task Force. The page gives no day for Sumatra's fall.

region.text: the Indies of 1941 after the surrender of 9 March 1942

ledger.note: 9 March 1942: the Dutch surrender Java and the Indies fall. Japanese troops landed at four points on northern Java between 28 February and 1 March; 'the Dutch commander and Governor General Tjarda surrendered' on 9 March (the page also gives 8 March). The Indies were then divided between the 16th Army (Java and Madura), the 25th Army (Sumatra) and the navy's 2nd South Fleet (Borneo and the east). The colony continued 'in exile (1942-1945)'.

region.text: the western half of New Guinea

ledger.note: 1944: Allied forces liberate much of Dutch New Guinea. 'MacArthur's Western New Guinea campaign liberated much of Dutch New Guinea' in 1944; the page does not say which parts stayed occupied.

region.text: the Sultanate of Yogyakarta

ledger.note: 1945: the Javanese principalities are disbanded. The Vorstenlanden infobox gives 'Disbanded: 1945'; Surakarta and Mangkunegaran were merged into Central Java in 1946.

region.text: the Sunanate of Surakarta

ledger.note: 1945: the Surakarta principality is disbanded (same page and infobox year).

region.text: Kalimantan and North Sulawesi

ledger.note: May-July 1945: the Allied Borneo campaign 'was fought to liberate British and Dutch Borneo'. The page gives no exact dates for the Borneo landings.

region.text: the Indies of 1941

ledger.note: 15 August 1945: Japan surrenders and the Dutch East Indies pass to the UK-led South East Asia Command that day. Indonesia's independence was proclaimed on 17 August; the occupation was formally disestablished on 12 September 1945 (infobox). Allied forces had bypassed Java and Sumatra, so most of the Indies were still occupied.

region.text: Jakarta, Medan, Padang, Palembang, Semarang and Surabaya

ledger.note: October 1945: British forces, with Dutch NICA troops, land in the Republic's cities. 'The first British troops reached Jakarta in late September 1945'; British troops reached Medan, Padang, Palembang, Semarang and Surabaya in October. The Netherlands 'did not return as a significant military force until early 1946'.

region.text: the Siak River basin round Siak Sri Indrapura (the page gives no extent; the sultanate-of-malacca dossier draws Siak as a 60 km disc here)

ledger.note: 1946: 'Sultan Syarif Kasim II, ceded his kingdom to the Republic of Indonesia in 1946 and encouraged other sultans to do likewise' (Siak page). Mirrors siak-sultanate /ledger/1 and /ledger/2 (loss and dissolve 1946, counterpart republic-of-indonesia); the Dutch protectorate over the coast ran on to 1949 elsewhere.

region.text: Jakarta, Medan, Padang, Palembang, Semarang and Surabaya

ledger.note: November 1946: the Linggadjati Agreement ends the first phase. It was 'concluded in November 1946'; the last British troops left that month and 55,000 Dutch troops had landed on Java (a citation-needed claim).

region.text: Java, Madura and Sumatra

ledger.note: November 1946: the Netherlands recognises the Republic as the de facto authority over Java, Madura and Sumatra at Linggadjati. In December 1946 the State of East Indonesia is set up at Makassar for the east.

region.text: East and West Java and parts of Sumatra

ledger.note: 20 July 1947: the Dutch launch Operation Product against the Republic (dated 21 July-5 August).

region.text: East and West Java and parts of Sumatra

ledger.note: 4 August 1947: a ceasefire called for by UN Security Council resolution 27 is ordered by the Dutch and Sukarno.

union.text: East and West Java and parts of Sumatra

parts of Sumatra, and East and West Java, from which 'Dutch forces drove Republican troops out' in Operation Product; the region is the difference between Cliopatria's 1946 and 1947 Republic shapes (Aceh, which the Dutch never invaded, is left out)

region.text: East and West Java and parts of Sumatra together with the land the Republic loses in Operation Product (republic-of-indonesia ledger/6)

ledger.note: August 1947: Dutch forces hold the plantation and port regions they took in Operation Product. They 'drove Republican troops out of parts of Sumatra, and East and West Java'; the Republic was 'confined to the Yogyakarta region of Java'. The Renville ceasefire line of January 1948 leaves it so. [fx-38 H43, 2026-11-01: the region is now Cliopatria's Dutch East Indies difference united with the region of republic-of-indonesia ledger/6, so the Republic's loss to dutch-east-indies is matched cell for cell (the Cliopatria difference alone missed 7 cells of it). Indonesian National Revolution page: 'Dutch forces drove Republican troops out of parts of Sumatra, and East and West Java' (Operation Product, launched at midnight on 20 July 1947); 'The Republicans were confined to the Yogyakarta region of Java'.]

region.text: Republican Java and Sumatra

ledger.note: 19 December 1948: Operation Kraai. By the next day the Dutch had conquered Yogyakarta, the Republican capital.

union.text: the Republic's remaining Java (Yogyakarta, taken 'by the following day') and most of Sumatra, lost in Operation Kraai; the Emergency Government held on in West Sumatra; the region is the difference between Cliopatria's 1948 shape and the 1949 pocket plus West Sumatra and Aceh (which the Dutch never invaded)

region.text: Republican Java and Sumatra together with the land the Republic loses in Operation Kraai (republic-of-indonesia ledger/8)

ledger.note: December 1948: the Dutch hold the Republic's cities. 'By the end of December, all major Republican-held cities in Java and Sumatra were in Dutch hands' (page wording). [fx-38 H43, 2026-11-01: the region is now Cliopatria's Dutch East Indies difference united with the region of republic-of-indonesia ledger/8, so the Republic's loss to dutch-east-indies is matched cell for cell (the Cliopatria difference alone missed 1 cells of it). Indonesian National Revolution page: 'By the end of December, all major Republican held cities in Java and Sumatra were in Dutch hands' after Operation Kraai (19 December 1948; Yogyakarta taken by the next day); 'An emergency Republican government ... was established in West Sumatra'.]

region.text: Republican Java and Sumatra

ledger.note: 27 December 1949: the fighting ends with the transfer of sovereignty. The Round Table Conference sat from 23 August to 2 November 1949; Republican forces had held Yogyakarta for about six hours on 1 March 1949. The page gives no ceasefire date.

region.text: the Pontianak sultanate

ledger.note: 1949: the Pontianak sultanate leaves the Dutch East Indies. The Pontianak page has the Dutch-created Special Region of West Kalimantan formed on 28 October 1946 and the region joining the Republic of the United States of Indonesia before 5 April 1950; the sultanate ends in 1950 on the infobox.

region.text: the western half of New Guinea

ledger.note: 27 December 1949: Dutch New Guinea stays Dutch. The territory 'was established as a Dutch colony' when the rest of the Indies became Indonesia; the Netherlands recognised Indonesian sovereignty 'with the exception of Dutch New Guinea' (Indonesian National Revolution page: 'It would include all the territory of the former Dutch East Indies with the exception of Dutch New Guinea'; the Dutch New Guinea page has instead 'in 1949, when the rest of the Dutch East Indies became fully independent as Indonesia, the Dutch retained sovereignty over western New Guinea'), which it handed over in 1962-1963 (UN administration in October 1962, transfer on 1 May 1963).

minus.text: the western half of New Guinea

region.text: the former Dutch East Indies without Dutch New Guinea

ledger.note: 27 December 1949: the Netherlands transfers sovereignty over the Dutch East Indies to the United States of Indonesia. 'Sovereignty was formally transferred' on 27 December 1949 'with the exception of Dutch New Guinea'.

wars.name: Invasion of Java (1811)
wars.outcome: The British fleet landed at Cilincing on 4 August 1811, Batavia capitulated on 8 August and Janssens surrendered on 18 September; Britain held Java and Madura until it returned them to the Dutch in 1816 under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814.
wars.note: The Dutch side is recorded as the colony itself under Governor Janssens, who surrendered; the main page calls 1806-1816 a 'French and British interregnum', and the Kingdom of Holland has no dossier slug to name.

wars.name: Java War

zones.text: the mancanagara annexed from the Javanese courts

wars.outcome: Ended on 28 March 1830 with Diponegoro's arrest; afterwards the Dutch annexed the outlying mancanagara areas of the Javanese princely states and Yogyakarta kept roughly the boundary of today's special region.
wars.note: The main page dates the war 1825-30 and says it 'ended significant Javanese resistance'. The Java War page does not date the annexation of the mancanagara, so the ledger carries it as a 1830 gain at confidence 2.

wars.name: Padri War

zones.text: the Minangkabau highlands of West Sumatra

wars.outcome: The Dutch pushed the Padri out of Pagaruyung on 4 March 1822, conquered Lintau in August 1831, took Padang Lawas on 8 June 1835 and fully conquered Fort Bonjol on 16 August 1837, after which the Minangkabau highlands were Dutch.
wars.note: The Dutch East Indies page gives the war as 1821-38; the Padri War page used here dates the fall of Fort Bonjol to 16 August 1837. The Dutch Resident at Padang in 1821 (James du Puy) is the page's earliest Dutch act. The Dutch were allied to the Minangkabau adat leaders against the Padri on the page's account; the Padri have no dossier.

wars.name: Banjarmasin War

zones.text: the Banjar sultanate in South and Central Kalimantan

wars.outcome: 'The war ended with a Dutch victory in 1863'; the Dutch abolished the Sultanate of Banjarmasin and ruled it 'under direct control of Batavia'.
wars.note: Tamjid abdicated in June 1859, Hidayatullah surrendered in early 1862 and Antasari died on 11 October 1862; the page records sporadic fighting until 1905.

wars.name: Aceh War
wars.outcome: The infobox dates the war 1873-1904; the Dutch took the coast in 1873, the capital in January 1874 and had 'most of Aceh' under control by the end of 1904.
wars.note: The main Dutch East Indies page puts the Acehnese surrender in 1912 against the war page's 1904 end; the ledger follows the war page. Cliopatria adds the Aceh interior to its Dutch East Indies shape only in 1914.

wars.name: Japanese occupation of the Dutch East Indies

zones.text: the Indies of 1941 after the surrender of 9 March 1942

wars.outcome: Japan invaded on 10 January 1942 and the Dutch commander surrendered on 9 March 1942; the colony continued 'in exile (1942-1945)' until Japan's surrender on 15 August 1945.
wars.note: Allied forces had bypassed Java and Sumatra, so most of the Indies were still occupied in August 1945; the occupation was formally disestablished on 12 September 1945 (infobox).

wars.name: Indonesian National Revolution

zones.text: East and West Java and parts of Sumatra

wars.outcome: Linggadjati (November 1946) recognised the Republic as the de facto authority over Java, Madura and Sumatra; Operation Product (20 July 1947) and Operation Kraai (19 December 1948) took back its plantation, port and city areas; sovereignty was transferred on 27 December 1949 except for Dutch New Guinea.
wars.note: The zones are the three stages the ledger carries (the Linggadjati area, the Product gains, the Kraai gains), drawn as Cliopatria shape differences, not as lines on the page.

wars.name: Dutch interventions in Bali
wars.outcome: Expeditions in 1846 and 1848 failed, 'an 1849 intervention brought northern Bali under Dutch control', and Bali was 'subjugated with military conquests' in 1906 and April 1908.
wars.note: The page opened (the main Dutch East Indies article) gives no individual article name for these interventions, so the title is descriptive. The Karangasem lands went with Lombok in 1894.

certainty.note: Coasts, forts and Java were held; no page gives surveyed interior lines. The one dated line is the 1824 Anglo-Dutch division of the Malay world (sharp, along the Strait), and the page says 'By 1900 the archipelago was considered pacified' with direct rule extended 'from 1901 to 1910'.

Direct colonial rule throughout the archipelago; this rests on the page's 1901-1910 sweep, not on a surveyed border list. The interior of Borneo and New Guinea, and the treaties with Sarawak, North Borneo and Portuguese Timor, were not checked on any page opened (Cliopatria draws the lines).
Occupation zones of 1942-1945 and the Republic's changing front lines of 1945-1949 are not surveyed borders.

REPAIR OF 2026-10-19 (author's repair after the adversarial review; supersedes the earlier text where they differ). (1) Both sides of every dependency now carry the event: the suzerain's ledger names the vassal as counterpart (vassal_start/vassal_end) and the vassal's dossier names the suzerain, so the Dutch East Indies now records vassalage of Pontianak, Mempawah (1800-c.1820), Bima (1800-1905), Gowa (1800-1911), Bulungan (27 September 1834 - June 1878), Ternate (1800-1914), Tidore (1817-1905, occupation 1806-1811), Bacan (1817-1889), Siak (21 August 1862 - 1946) and the courts of Yogyakarta and Surakarta (1806-1811, 1816-1945). An occupation event names the occupier when this state is occupied (British, Japanese) and the occupied state when this state occupies (Tidore 1806-1811). (2) Convention for the keyframes: Cliopatria's Dutch East Indies shapes include land that was only a Dutch vassal (Pontianak, Gowa, Bulungan from 1853, the Moluccan sultanates from 1824, the courts); that land is kept in the shapes and carried by the vassal events, and a gain event marks the year the land passes to direct rule (the neighbour's end year). Land that was neither Dutch nor a vassal in a given year is removed from the keyframe until its gain (Mempawah 1828-1830, Bima's Flores lands 1890-1904, the Flores cells held by Portugal to 1859, the Siak basin 1857-1861). (3) Gains re-dated to the neighbours' pages: Sambas 1822 -> 1819 (Sambas page), Mempawah 1828 -> 1831 (Mempawah page), Kutai 1846 -> 1844 (Kutai page; counterpart kutai-kingdom, which holds the Cliopatria row 'Sultanate of Kutai Kartanegara'), Bima 1890 -> 1905 (Bima page); new gains: Pagaruyung's Luhak Tanah Datar 2 May 1833, Karangasem 1894 and Badung 1906 from Bali, Bulungan June 1878, Gowa 1911, Bacan 1889, Tidore 1905, Ternate 1914, Flores and Solor from Portugal 20 April 1859 (ratified 18 August 1860), Luwu and Wajo 1905 (confidence 1: the page names them as targets without dates); contest events added for the north Bali expeditions (1846-1849) and the Padri War (April 1821-1824, 1831-16 August 1837).
